steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Raising agents introduce gas into mixtures, creating bubbles that expand during cooking, making products light and airy. There are three types: mechanical, chemical, and biological.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Mechanical aeration: physically incorporating air — whisking (eggs + sugar in sponge), creaming (butter + sugar in cakes), folding (retaining air when adding flour), rolling (puff pastry layers).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Steam: water turns to steam at 100°C, expanding dramatically (1700x volume). Steam raises Yorkshire puddings, choux pastry, and puff pastry. The initial burst of high heat creates rapid steam production.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Chemical raising agents: bicarbonate of soda (NaHCO₃) and baking powder (bicarbonate + cream of tartar). They produce carbon dioxide gas when activated.
